results/preregistration.json.description: Every hypothesis with its numeric threshold and falsifier, written before any measurement exists. analyze.py may only compare against this file.

fields.name: hypotheses[].claim
fields.meaning: which lettered claim it belongs to

results/provenance.json.description: Run identity: git, versions, model digests, machine, allowlisted env.

fields.name: ollama.pinned_models.<name>.digest
fields.meaning: THE load-bearing pin: the tag is mutable, the digest is not

fields.name: git.dirty
fields.meaning: whether the working tree had uncommitted changes

fields.name: environment_allowlisted
fields.meaning: only DOCUMENT_STORE_DIR / OLLAMA_BASE_URL / TZ / LANG — never the full environ

data/REGISTRY.json.description: Per-paper input provenance. Committed; data/pdfs/ is gitignored.

fields.name: papers[].sha256
fields.meaning: content hash of the downloaded PDF

results/data_integrity.json.description: Re-hash of every registered PDF. Exits 1 on drift.

fields.name: checks[].ok
fields.meaning: sha256 and size both match the registry

results/conversion_baseline.json.description: Standalone harvest.extract per PDF: the markdown corpus, and the per-PDF conversion cost that prices the checkpoint.

fields.name: conversions[].markdown_sha256
fields.meaning: valid WITHIN a docling version only — never compared across runs

results/gate_llm.json.description: H-G. The blocking precondition that the LLM really enriches.

fields.name: extract_chunk_metadata_seconds
fields.meaning: a sub-second value is the signature of the swallowed-provider-error path

results/claim_a_defer.json.description: H-a1..H-a5: defer is LLM-free, fast, findable — but not for sources.

results/claim_e_pre.json.description: Claim (e) control arm + the auto_repair tripwire.

fields.name: pre_chunk_recall_at_3
fields.meaning: must be 0 — there are no chunks yet

fields.name: fingerprint_moved
fields.meaning: tripwire: search()'s auto_repair must not drain

results/claim_b_drain.json.description: H-b: resumable, and a no-op drain is genuinely a no-op.

results/claim_e_post.json.description: H-e1/H-e2: the drain created semantic reachability.

fields.name: doc_embedding_skip_rate
fields.meaning: MEASURED not asserted — _embed_doc_level swallows oversized input

results/micro_stages.json.description: Sequential attribution of enrichment, and the fan-out ratio.

fields.name: concurrency_speedup
fields.meaning: sequential total / in-pipeline seconds; ~1.0 means Semaphore(5) is decoration

results/claim_c_kill.json.description: The SIGKILL, the gate that opened it, and the post-kill truth.

results/claim_c_resume.json.description: H-c1/H-c2/H-c3/H-d4 and the checkpoint's price in seconds.

fields.name: ledger_entries
fields.meaning: MUST equal the number of sources

fields.name: checkpoint_savings_seconds
fields.meaning: conversion seconds not repeated, taken from THIS lineage's own converter-ledger entry. INCLUDES one-time Docling initialisation (that conversion was first in its process); the measured warm cost and docling_init_seconds sit in checkpoint_savings_basis so the marginal saving is legible

fields.name: repeated_enrichment_seconds
fields.meaning: MEASURED on this lineage: killed_at minus the converter ledger's last ts_end — the enrichment the resume must redo. Previously this field copied micro_stages' sequential total, a different paper in a different database

fields.name: repeated_enrichment_over_conversion
fields.meaning: H-d4's second threshold: repeated enrichment must cost less than the conversion the checkpoint preserved

fields.name: reconciliation.n_mismatches
fields.meaning: H-x for the subprocess resume drain, which previously bypassed it

results/claim_d_pause.json.description: Four pause mechanisms, all stopping between documents.

fields.name: pause_midstage_documents
fields.meaning: MUST be empty (H-d1). Union over EACH ARM'S OWN post-drain snapshot of rows that are 'failed' or carry chunk/chunk-embedding rows while not 'complete'. Computed per arm on purpose: the snapshot after the final unrestricted drain would have repaired exactly this

fields.name: pause_discarded_seconds
fields.meaning: MEASURED: wall-clock each library arm spent after its last committed document, summed. Not a constant

fields.name: pause_discarded_document_fraction
fields.meaning: the worst arm's post-commit seconds over that drain's own longest single-document cost — H-d1's scored secondary threshold

fields.name: sigterm_to_exit_seconds
fields.meaning: ARM 5: measured with an UNTRUNCATED document in flight. THIS is the number that sizes a launchd/cron shutdown grace period

fields.name: sigterm_to_exit_seconds_truncated
fields.meaning: ARM 4: the same measurement on a 6000-char truncation (~2 chunks). Reported for contrast ONLY — NOT operational guidance

fields.name: sigterm_in_flight_document
fields.meaning: size of the document arm 5 committed while the signal was in flight, which is what makes the latency interpretable

results/claim_f_fail.json.description: H-f1/H-f2: failures recorded and diagnosable; retry routes by stage.

fields.name: failure_fidelity[].exception_type
fields.meaning: what a UI can match on

fields.name: stage_test_converter_calls
fields.meaning: ALL conversions in the stage-test drain, including the still-broken sources that correctly return to pending_source

fields.name: stage_test_converter_calls_good_doc
fields.meaning: conversions of the MARKDOWN-BEARING document — MUST be 0 (H-f2)

results/drain_overhead.json.description: The fixed preflight tax a cron-driven drain pays on every wake-up.

results/claims.json.description: One row per hypothesis: threshold, measured value, verdict.

results/validation.json.description: Schema + referential-integrity validation of every results file.

fields.name: violations
fields.meaning: empty means valid; any entry exits 1

results/events.jsonl.description: Every OBSERVED queue transition, concatenated in rule order. TRAP: documents_skipped uses `continue` WITHOUT incrementing `done`, so on_progress never fires for a skipped source and `done` can end below `total`.

fields.name: benchmark_wall_seconds
fields.meaning: process wall time from Snakemake's benchmark:. Populated for EVERY rule and one single quantity, so it is the only column safe to plot on one axis. Its memory/IO columns are literally 0 on this macOS host and are NOT measurements

fields.name: in_script_component_seconds
fields.meaning: in-script time.monotonic, populated only where an artefact carries one. NOT commensurable across rules — for micro_stages it is a SUM OF COMPONENTS, elsewhere a single drain — which is why it is not plotted

fields.name: in_script_component_meaning
fields.meaning: which of those two the value is, stated per row

fields.name: max_in_flight_global
fields.meaning: whole-process depth over all endpoints; per-endpoint peaks live in each artefact's http.max_in_flight_by_path

results/per_document.csv.description: One row per document in the main lineage after the drain.

fields.name: llm_metadata_populated
fields.meaning: persistent trace of the H-G failure

results/MANIFEST.json.description: Every artefact with sha256, bytes, producing rule and schema.

fields.name: harness_sha256
fields.meaning: one digest over Snakefile + config.yaml + every scripts/*.py

results/deviations.json.description: Every change to a hypothesis, metric, threshold or scoring rule made AFTER a measurement was observed. A pre-registration that can be edited after the fact with no amendment trail provides the appearance of the guarantee rather than the guarantee.

fields.name: deviations[].could_have_moved_the_verdict
fields.meaning: the honest direction: harder, easier, or neutral

results/cli_smoke.json.description: Every andamentum-docstore subcommand run through the venv console script: exit code, stdout shape, and `status` output parsed back and compared with the database.

fields.name: status_database_counts
fields.meaning: the same counts read straight from sqlite — must agree

results/ledgers/*_convert.jsonl.format: JSONL, one object per line, append-only, fsynced before return
results/ledgers/*_convert.jsonl.description: ONE LINE PER convert_fn INVOCATION. The load-bearing instrument for the checkpoint claim: 'conversion is not repeated' reduces to a line count a reader can verify by opening a text file. fsynced before the wrapper returns, which is what makes it valid evidence under a SIGKILL.

fields.name: source
fields.meaning: the path or URL converted; DUPLICATES FALSIFY H-c1

fields.name: pid
fields.meaning: which process converted it — kill vs resume

fields.name: chars
fields.meaning: length of the markdown produced; 0 on error

fields.name: sha256
fields.meaning: hash of the markdown; H-c2 compares it

fields.name: error_type
fields.meaning: exception class name, or null on success

results/ledgers/*_http.jsonl.produced_by: every measurement rule (one ledger per arm)
results/ledgers/*_http.jsonl.format: JSONL, one object per httpx request, appended in completion order
results/ledgers/*_http.jsonl.description: Every HTTP request the recording process made, with in-flight depth at start. H-a1 (defer is LLM-free) is the emptiness of one of these files.

fields.name: global_depth_at_start
fields.meaning: requests open across ALL endpoints when this one started — an upper bound on any single endpoint, never an attribution

fields.name: in_flight_at_start_path
fields.meaning: requests open ON THIS PATH when this one started — the per-endpoint concurrency figure

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: HTTP status, or null if the request raised

results/snapshots/*.json.produced_by: drain.instrumented_drain (pre and post, one pair per drain)
results/snapshots/*.json.description: The complete read-only observation of one database at one instant: the logical fingerprint, status counts, and a full row dump. Every headline count in this experiment is re-derivable from these offline.

fields.name: label
fields.meaning: which drain and which side (pre / post)

fields.name: logical_fingerprint
fields.meaning: sha256 over the MEANING of every row (uuid|status|file_hash|markdown_len|n_chunks|has_doc_embedding|n_chunk_embeddings|metadata_keys). The file hash is not used: WAL checkpoints move bytes without changing meaning

fields.name: file_advisory
fields.meaning: byte-level facts, ADVISORY — nothing asserts on them

results/events/*.jsonl.produced_by: each claim rule (one file per rule)
results/events/*.jsonl.format: JSONL, one observed transition per line
results/events/*.jsonl.description: The per-rule event log merged by `merge_events` into results/events.jsonl and events.csv. Same field set as that merged file.

results/events.csv.description: The flat rendering of results/events.jsonl, same fields.

results/working_tree.patch.description: WRITTEN ONLY WHEN THE TREE IS DIRTY, and REQUIRED whenever git.dirty is true. A recorded sha with dirty=true and no diff names code that cannot be recovered — the previous edition of this run was measured against an uncommitted one-line fix without which it crashes.

figures/figures_status.json.description: Per-figure success/failure. Consulted by build_report, which prints a visible FIGURE COULD NOT BE DRAWN line rather than embedding a placeholder as though it were a result.

fields.name: figures[].ok
fields.meaning: false means the file is a placeholder

fields.name: figures[].error
fields.meaning: type and message when not ok
